newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends up on export inspections.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends up on export inspections.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed higher and up from their intraday lows on ideas of oversold conditions and on support from USDA's higher-than-expected export inspection number, traders said.
USDA said 33.588 million bushels of wheat were inspected for export during the week ended Sept 5 -- well above trade expectations for 22.0 million to 26.0 million bushels.

"We just ran out of momentum to the downside. Our wheat's been beaten pretty bad in here lately and I think we just saw some unwinding of positions ahead of (the release of the USDA's September crop report) on Wednesday," a trader said.
Traders said CIS sold one million Dec bushels and Benson Quinn sold 1.3 million Dec. Atwood-Peavey reportedly bought 1.2 million Dec.
MGE spring wheat closed 1/4 to 5-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with Sept up 5-3/4 cents at $4.52. Dec closed up 1-1/2 cents at $4.30-3/4 per bushel.
The MGE estimated Monday's spring wheat volume at 16.487 million bushels, down from Friday's estimate of 22.20 million bushels.
MGE barley futures closed steady to four cents per hundredweight lower, with Sept unchanged at $7.40 per cwt.
